title: Kaleidoscope: In-language Exams for Massively Multilingual Vision Evaluation
claim: A benchmark spans many languages, subjects and modalities, shown through sample questions and its composition breakdowns.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; sample questions, language bars, stacked category bars
description: A three-panel figure. Panel (a) on the left shows two example multiple-choice questions in rounded colored cards. The first is a Reasoning question that asks for the number of triangles in a line drawing. The second is a Literature question that asks the reader to match excerpts with their authors. Each question has A to D answer pills, and the correct one is highlighted in green. Panel (b), in the middle, is a horizontal bar chart of the number of samples for 18 languages, from Portuguese down to Nepali. Each bar is split into multimodal (dark gray) and text-only (pale blue). Panel (c), on the right, has one 100% stacked bar per language, aligned with the rows in (b). The bars are colored by subject category, such as STEM (green), Arts & Humanities (purple), Social Sciences (yellow), Reasoning (blue), Health Sciences (gray) and Practical Skills (orange). A legend sits below the bars. The eye goes first to the colorful question cards and then to the bar charts.
caption: Overview of the Kaleidoscope Benchmark. (a) Multilingual-Multimodal MCQ Samples (b) Language and Multimodal Samples Distribution. (c) Exam Category Breakdown.
abstract: The evaluation of vision-language models (VLMs) has mainly relied on English-language benchmarks, leaving significant gaps in both multilingual and multicultural coverage. While multilingual benchmarks have expanded, both in size and languages, many rely on translations of English datasets, failing to capture cultural nuances. In this work, we propose Kaleidoscope, as the most comprehensive exam benchmark to date for the multilingual evaluation of vision-language models. Kaleidoscope is a large-scale, in-language multimodal benchmark designed to evaluate VLMs across diverse languages and visual inputs. Kaleidoscope covers 18 languages and 14 different subjects, amounting to a total of 20,911 multiple-choice questions. Built through an open science collaboration with a diverse group of researchers worldwide, Kaleidoscope ensures linguistic and cultural authenticity. We evaluate top-performing multilingual vision-language models and find that they perform poorly on low-resource languages and in complex multimodal scenarios. Our results highlight the need for progress on culturally inclusive multimodal evaluation frameworks.
